CITY OF INGLEWOOD

1 West Manchester Boulevard

  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS
Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social
distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to Assembly
Bill 361, please note that members of the public will only be allowed
to observe and address the Planning Commission of March 2, 2022 at
7:00 P.M. by telephone, video and other means, as follows:

Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members
of the public may listen and make oral public comments
telephonically by dialing:

  Phone Number: 888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694
  Access Code: 5037512#

Please observe the following tips when phoning in:
   When you call-in, the operator will provide further
  instructions on how you can make public comments via phone.
   If you are calling from a cell phone, please call from an area
  with good reception.
   If you are watching the meeting on Facebook or Channel 35 while
  also accessing the phone line, it is requested that you mute the
  sound of your video feed as it is offset by 3 seconds from the
  phone transmission. Additionally, when you are making public
  comments on the phone line you will be inaudible due to feedback.

Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:
   On Spectrum Cable Local Channel 35 with audio and limited video.
  Please check with your cable provider for details.
   Live on-line through Facebook Live, with audio and limited
  video, at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

Written Public Comments: Members of the public can submit comments
for consideration by the Planning Commission by sending them to Mindy
Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager at mwilcox@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Planning Commission prior
to consideration of the agenda, comments must be received prior to
12:00 P.M. on March 2, 2022 the day of the meeting. Correspondence
should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received
after 12:00 P.M. and prior to close of the public hearing will be
made part of the official public record of the meeting.

Accessibility: If you will require special accommodations due to a
disability, please contact the Planning Division Office at (310) 412-
5230, One Manchester Boulevard, 4th Floor, Inglewood, California
90301.  All requests for accommodations must be received 48 hours
prior to the day of the hearing.

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, MARCH 2, 2022

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:
The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, March 2, 2022, in the City Council
Chambers, on the ninth floor, of City Hall. Following the Pledge
of Allegiance by Commissioner Aidé Trejo, the meeting was called
to order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:
Present: Chairman Larry Springs
  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide Trejo
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams

Staff:  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., ECDD Director
  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner
  Arturo Salazar, Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Planner
  Angel Leon-Martell, Assistant Planner
  Christine Rivera, Assistant Planner
  Michael Pan, Assistant City Attorney
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary
  Louis Atwell, Assistant City Manager/Public Works Dir.
  Via Community Phone Call Coverage:
  AT&T Conference Call Operator Rep.

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:
Ms. Wilcox, Planning Manager noted a few corrections on the Agenda.
In regards to the Minutes, the correct minutes are included in
your packets, with the corrected dates of December 1, 2021; January
18, 2022; and February 2, 2022; additionally for Item 6A, the
division has received several comment letters in support and copies
have been distributed to each of the Planning Commissioners and
have been posted on-line; last there is a revised Mitigation
Monitoring and Reporting Program, that has been posted on-line and
distributed to each of the Planning Commissioners.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None (Confirmed by AT&T Operator).

(5) MINUTES APPROVAL:
Motion made by Commissioner Rice to vote on all of the Minutes
covering December 1, 2021, January 18, 2022 and February 2, 2022
all at one time since every planning commissioner was present at
each hearing and the motion was seconded by Commissioner Patrick.

The motion passed with the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Commissioner Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs.

Motion made by Commissioner Rice to Approve the Minutes of December
1, 2021, January 18, 2022 and February 2, 2022 and was seconded by
Commissioner Trejo.

The motion passed with the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Commissioner Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs.
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 2, 2022

(6) PUBLIC HEARINGS:
Chairman Springs is requested a motion of the Planning Commission
to move Item 6A to the last hearing position for tonight’s meeting.

Motion made by Commissioner Trejo to move Item 6A to the last
hearing position and move Items 6B and 7A forward. The motion was
seconded by Commissioner Patrick.

The motion passed with the following roll call vote:
Yeas:  Commissioner Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs.

6B: SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2022-002 (SP-2022-002), 220 NORTH LA
BREA AVENUE.
A public hearing to consider an application by Beth Aboulafia
representing Target Corporation for Special Use Permit No. 2022-
002 (SP-2022-002) to allow the sale of beer and wine for off-site
consumption in an approximately 35,000 square-foot one-story
retail tenant space that is part of a multiple tenant mixed use
development on an approximately 2.77-acre site at 220 North La
Brea Avenue and legally described as Lots 1 through 32 of Block
305 (APN 4015-028-013 thru 023), 220 North La Brea Avenue.

Mr. Art Salazar, Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff,

Commissioner Trejo asked the staff if there will be both non-
refrigerated as well as refrigerated alcohol at this location and
in the aisles.
  - Mr. Salazar responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.

Chairman Springs then asked the applicant to address the Planning
Commission and speak about their project.

Ms. Beth Aboulafia, Representative for Target, Inc., addressed the
Planning Commission via the telephone and spoke about her project.

Commissioner Patrick asked the applicant several questions, first
asked in regards to the possibility that there will be a food court
area, along with a CVS or other medical based services within this
particular Target,
  - Ms. Aboulafia responded to Commissioner Patrick’s question.

Commissioner Rice asked the applicant about the size of the Beer
and Wine section in this Target store, if it is the same size as
the Century Boulevard Target Store,
   Mr. Christopher E. Jackson responded to Commissioner Rice’s
  question.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant what will this store do
with regard to Security, especially with a lot of smash and grab
situations, which is at this particular location and will there be
a certain protocol?
  - Ms. Aboulafia responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked the applicant regarding the
cleaning maintenance of the store, both inside and outside.
   Ms. Aboulafia responded to Commissioner Shaw-Williams’
  questions.

  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 2, 2022
Chairman Springs asked the applicant several questions regarding
the way the Beer and Wine will be sold, in individual cans and
bottles or in cases?
   Ms. Aboulafia responded to Commissioner Shaw-Williams
  questions.

Chairman Springs opened the public hearing to the audience to
speak either for or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST:
None (Confirmed by the AT&T Operator).

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and asked for any

Condition number 17 regarding the word “serving” and if can be

(7) NON-PUBLIC HEARING:

7A: DESIGN REVIEW 2022-004 (DR-2022-004) FOR 3000 WEST MANCHESTER
BOULEVARD.
A non-public hearing to consider an approximately 1,200 square-
foot on-site mural on the exterior of an existing one-story
commercial building on an approximately 11,996 square-foot
property C-2 (General Commercial) zoned property at 3000 West
Manchester Boulevard

Ms. Christine  Rivera,  Assistant  Planner,  made  the  staff

  3
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 2, 2022
Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff. Seeing none he called for the applicant to
address the Commissioners.

Mr. Paul Seo, the applicant, addressed the Planning Commission.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for the applicant.

Commissioner Patrick stated –
 For all who may not know, this building initially was the Whitman
  Mayo Travel Agency Service building, and Whitman Mayo played
  the character Grady on Sanford & Son.
 My question for the applicant is if they will be utilizing anti-
  graffiti paint for the mural and will there be constant
  maintenance of the mural, for touch-ups frequently?
  - Mr. Seo responded to Commissioner Patrick’s question.

Commissioner Rice stated –
 Congratulations and applause on what you are addressing with
  your Mural, the message is good, but not too thrilled about the
  design proposed. Feels there could have been a better design
  chosen.

Commissioner Trejo stated –
 Thank you for clarification as to why the mural is being proposed
  – the 30th Anniversary of the L.A. Riots.
 Question regarding the funding from Superintendent Holly
  Mitchell, how did that process come about?
 Are there other murals within Supt. Mitchell’s district, which
  is why she chose to fund this project?
  - Mr. Seo responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams stated –
 Thank you for the clarification as to why the mural. Likes the
  design.

Chairman Springs stated –
 Also wanted to say thanks for the clarification of the purpose
  of the mural, also, what is being presented, will that be what
  will be painted?
 Last, remembers the Whitman Mayo Travel Agency Service, utilized
  it personally, great service.
  - Mr. Seo responded to Chairman Springs’ question.

Mr. Seo wanted to just tell the supervisors of Planner Marissa
Fewell, and Assistant Planner Christine Rivera, what a great and
excellent job they both did with keeping Mr. Seo on track and their
assistance with making sure his project went before the planning
commission.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
further questions for the applicant, seeing none called for a
motion.

seconded by Commissioner Shaw-Williams, that Resolution No. 1922

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeal process.

6A: INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR PROJECT.
A public hearing to consider the following matters associated with the
Inglewood Transit Connector Project:

a.  Environmental Impact Report EA-EIR-2018-073 (EA-EIR-2018-073)
  to assess the proposed Inglewood Transit Connector Project
  effect on the environment;
b.  General Plan Amendment No. 2022-001 (GPA-2022-001) to modify
  the Land Use, Safety and Circulation Elements of the Inglewood
  General Plan for the Inglewood Transit Connector Project; and
c.  Zone Change No. 2022-001 (ZC-2022-001) to establish a
  Transportation Corridor Overlay Zone;
d.  Zoning Code Amendment No. 2022-001 (ZCA-2022-001) to make
  modification to Chapter 12 of the Inglewood Municipal Code
  (Planning and Zoning) related to the Inglewood Transit
  Connector Project;
e.  Design Standards and Guidelines for the Inglewood Transit
  Connector Project.

Mr. Louis Atwell, Assistant City Manager, Public Works Director,
introduced Ms. Lisa Trifiletti of Trifiletti Consulting to make
the presentation on behalf of the Public Works Department.

Ms. Lisa Trifiletti concluded the staff presentation, along with
several staff from Trifiletti Consulting, Mr. Sanjeev Shah, SSI;
and Ms. Ellen Wright, addressed the Planning Commission.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for the applicant.

Commissioner Patrick asked Ms. Trifiletti –
 In reading your materials, have you considered the impact your
  construction will have on the McCormick Ambulance Service,
  Station No. 9, that is located across from the Vons’ Market to
  the west, and have you thought to relocate that service, so as
  to not disrupt their business, as they are a very busy and
  active at that site
   Ms. Trifiletti she had not considered that Ambulance service
  there, but will be happy to look into it.

  5
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 2, 2022
Commissioner Rice asked Ms. Trifiletti –
 The width of the platform of the people mover, how wide is it,
 What is the height off the ground?
 How many parking spaces will be provided?
 Will there be added parking spaces or structure created?
 Manchester and Market Street to Nutwood an additional stop to
  allow riders the opportunity to stop and shop at the local
  businesses there?
  - Ms. Trifiletti requested one of her technical staff, Mr.
  Sanjeev Shah to reply to Commissioner Rice’s question.
   Mr. Shah replied that the platform would be 30 to 35 feet
  wide, in some sections 27 to 32 feet wide. The height is about
  40 feet high.
   Ms. Trifiletti stated that there will be no closure of Market
  Street, but there will be additional parking at the CVS site,
  no parking structure will be implemented.
   Ms. Trifiletti stated there are no current plans for a fourth
  stop at that location, but it can be looked at.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant several questions –
 Glad to hear that there is an assistance program for all of the
  small businesses.
 How will the businesses be made aware of what assistance is
  being offered and how will they qualify to be helped them during
  the construction phases and the building phases?
 Noticed that there was a concern from one business owner, Mr.
  Raymont Johnson, a dentist had several questions regarding what
  will be the impact on his business during the construction of
  the project, will you reach out to assist him and others like
  him?
 What about dual language for both Spanish and English, or for
  anyone whose first language is not English? Will you address
  this issue?
  - Ms. Trifiletti stated that there will also be a liaison
  team for those businesses. Stated that it is required that
  in partnership with L.A. Metro, there is a service agreement
  with them to utilize their staff and resources to aide these
  businesses.
  - Ms. Trifiletti stated that definitely they will reach out not
  only to Mr. Johnson, but to all of the businesses along the
  rail route.
  - Ms. Trifiletti stated that it will be no problem to address
  most of the languages in the City and they will make sure
  that everyone will be able to understand the information.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked Ms. Trifiletti –
 Clarification, did you say that the Crenshaw line will now be
  called the “K” line?
 Eventually connecting to the Green Line in the future?
 Planet Fitness at that Vons’ Market building, what will happen
  with that location? Looking to close it?
  - Ms. Trifiletti stated that Metro has renamed their rail lines
  and is now calling the Crenshaw line, the “K” line.
  - Ms. Trifiletti stated that the idea is that to have a fully
  connected City, in the future to eventually connect the
  rail throughout the City.
  - Ms. Trifiletti stated that Von’ Market is trying to decide
  what they are going to do with that portion of the building,
  as during Covid-19, that side of the building was closed and
  not in use, so it will be up to Vons.

  6
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 2, 2022
Chairman Springs then asked Ms. Trifiletti –
 He stated his question had to do with the Gas Station that
  located in the Vons parking lot, will it be removed or relocated?
 On Nutwood and Hillcrest, there is a new construction going on
  there and it will be a mixed use building, will the rail project
  have any effect on the project that is on at that building which
  is on the back-side of the Vons’ Market?
 On Prairie, you stated that in order to not disrupt the school,
  your project is going to take over the corner of Prairie Avenue
  and Manchester Boulevard, where you will take over the lot there
  on the corner, is it possible that both you and the Raisin’ Cane
  operation will share that location?
 With regards to Prairie Avenue, my question is about the
  sidewalks and how it appears to be not as wide as it is nearer
  to Manchester Boulevard, so as you continue south, they appear
  to be getting smaller.
 Your last stop which will be at Hardy and Prairie, and that
  location is a strip mall, where there are multiple tenants. This
  stop will displace those tenants, will you cover those tenants
  lease, for the balance of their lease and will you relocate
  them?
 With regards to the McCormick’s Ambulance Emergency Service, as
  they will need to be able to get in and out quickly in order to
  conduct their business, will it be possible that you get
  together with them to determine what they will need in order to
  easily enter and depart successfully?
   Ms. Trifiletti stated that it would fully be up to the Vons’
  Market, but that at this time the Gas Station will be removed.
   Ms. Trifiletti stated that it would not have anything to do
  with the mixed-use project at all.
   Ms. Trifiletti stated that it would have been nice to share
  the location with the Raisin’ Cane Restaurant, but that
  Raisin’ Cane felt that it was not what their franchise is
  looking to do at the present time, but will be looking to
  doing business in the City of Inglewood, just somewhere else.
   Ms. Trifiletti deferred this question to Ellen Wright,
  Trifiletti Consulting Rep.
   Ms. Wright stated that Chairman Springs is correct, the
  sidewalk does narrow significantly going south on Prairie
  Avenue and in looking at the width of the sidewalks, in
  relation to the transit facilities, and in some cases based
  on today’s scale they will be made a little wider, but in no
  way will they ever be made narrower than present days width,
  to make sure the streetscape is enhanced for the pedestrian
  walking experience overall.
   Ms. Trifiletti stated that as the daughter of parents who
  were small business owners, she wanted to make sure that each
  business in that mall were well aware ahead of any periodicals
  that may come out and were comfortable with what the new
  project would entail. She stated she wanted each business
  owner to know and have a face and a person to contact if they
  had any questions or concerns. So far, she has established
  real relationships with all of the business owners and she
  has found out exactly what each business will need in order
  for that business to stay afloat.
   Ms. Trifiletti stated that they have access to relocation
  specialist on this program who will be working with each of
  the businesses, taking in all their information and surveys
  of what each business will need. Help with all the legal
  steps.
   Ms. Trifiletti stated that will not be a problem, and she
  will make sure that the Ambulance Service will be addressed
  and taken care of.
  7
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 2, 2022
Commissioner Patrick asked Ms. Trifiletti –
 When will you and your company come out to talk to the
  residents, as rumors are flying rampant all over the city, my
  neighbors can’t even have a decent event at their homes because
  of the fears they have over the rumors.
   Ms. Trifiletti stated that initially, they conducted town
  halls, and get to know events throughout the City, along
  with internet, emails, and flyers, but since Covid-19, all
  in-person meetings had been cancelled, there had been quite
  a few zoom meetings. She stated that it can appear scary
  with misinformation being presented by people who don’t
  truly know the full facts. We do have a newsletter along
  with a website and now that more and more people are being
  vaccinated, we will and can do more to make sure that the
  truth gets out to the public.
Commissioner Rice asked Ms. Trifiletti several questions –
 80 parking spaces located at the Hardy and Prairie station,
  but what about Game Day, will parking costs be the same as
  normal non-Game day rates for the general parking users?
 What about the parking opportunity like only having to pay
  $15.00 per day and ride all day?
 Another question for clarification, with regards to the details
  to the actual track on Market Street, where exactly will the
  people mover tracks be located, will it be in the middle of
  the street, and what about down Prairie Avenue it appears to
  be on the west side of the street?
 What is the column width and cost per column and will this
  make Prairie Avenue narrower with the addition of the Rail
  line?
  - Ms. Trifiletti stated that she was not sure of what the fees
  would be during a game/work day of park and ride. It is
  something they can and will look into.
  - Ms. Trifiletti stated that is a true observation, its one
  thing to have the people mover utilized during game days, but
  what about the remainder of the year and the community at
  large?
  - Ms. Trifiletti asked Mr. Shah to reply to this question, but
  also stated that the purpose in their design is to make sure
  that pedestrian traffic has full access to the sky and are
  not overshadowed by the people mover.
  - Mr. Shah stated that Prairie Avenue has the most numbers of
  utilities – other than Century Boulevard, and in order to not
